Edge Perception Reliability Lab
workbench / overview
GitHub
Object detection · adverse weather · local workbench

Does a detector trained on clear roads still work in fog, snow and night?

A pretrained detector that works on a sunny demo clip says little about the night, fog or snow. This lab runs YOLOX-Nano on real adverse-weather driving frames from SeeingThroughFog and scores it against human labels, condition by condition. It also applies controlled synthetic degradations and measures how detections change, then puts the two side by side to ask whether simulated fog damages the detector the way real fog does.

View the code on GitHub github.com/Khriis-K/Edge-Perception-Reliability-Lab

Two modes, one question

clean input and predictionsdegraded input and predictions
Benchmark mode

Real weather, scored against human labels

Reads a local copy of SeeingThroughFog (Bijelic et al., CVPR 2020), assigns every frame one of eight conditions from the refined metadata, draws a seeded subset and computes AP per class and mAP per condition.

Synthetic mode

Controlled degradations, measured against the clean run

Applies darkness, blur, fog, noise or JPEG compression at a chosen severity and seed, to a video or to clear dataset frames, and measures how detections shift. The sim-to-real view sets the AP drop under synthetic fog beside the drop under real fog.

Headline finding: under investigation

The first real sim-to-real comparison has been run, but on that subset real fog appears to raise overall mAP, which isn't physically plausible. The result is being checked before any number is stated (issue #57).

What the workbench does

Dataset adapter

Maps refined metadata to clear, fog, snow and rain, each split day and night. Ambiguous samples (fog with snow, twilight, contradicting flags, incomplete metadata) are excluded and counted, never guessed.

Reproducible subsets

The same seed, cap and dataset always draw the same subset. A manifest of frame ids (never images) can be downloaded, committed and rerun; the app refuses one from another vocabulary version.

Frame inspection

Clean and degraded detections side by side, a per-frame match table, and worst frames ranked by a score that shows every contributing value next to it.

Latency panel

Per-stage p50 and p90 timing with warm-up excluded, effective fps, and the ONNX Runtime execution provider recorded with every run (CPU or CUDA).

Run cache

Each run is keyed by everything that affects its results, so the same settings reuse cached results across restarts. Cancelled or failed runs are never cached.

Reports

Findings export as HTML, JSON and CSV. Every report includes the class-mapping definition and leaves dataset frames out by default, referring to them by id.

Two metric families, never mixed up

A video clip has no labels, so calling its numbers "accuracy" would be wrong. The lab keeps stability against the clean run separate from accuracy against ground truth, with every rule written down.

Stability · vs the clean run

Detections at confidence ≥ 0.25, matched greedily at IoU ≥ 0.5.

  • retainedsame class on both sides
  • class changeoverlapping, but a different class
  • droppeda clean detection with no match
  • introduceda degraded detection with no match
Accuracy · vs human labels

Predictions taken in descending confidence, per frame.

  • hittakes the best-overlapping unmatched object of its class, IoU ≥ 0.5
  • confusiontakes an unmatched object of another class
  • ignoredat least half its area inside an ignore region
  • false alarmany other prediction; unmatched objects are misses
Sample-size honesty

Every metric shows its object and frame counts and is flagged low n below 30 objects. On video, consecutive frames of one object aren't independent evidence, so the flag under-warns there, and an ADR records that.

Worst-frame score
misses + false alarms + class confusions
dropped + introduced + class changes + confidence loss

Benchmark, then Synthetic. Losing a full 1.0 of confidence weighs as much as one dropped detection.

The committed benchmark subset

The real Benchmark run uses seed 0 and a cap of 300 frames per condition. Its manifest is committed, so anyone with the dataset can rerun exactly these frames. Conditions with fewer qualifying samples than the cap fall short of it.

Engineering work

Latency · time.perf_counter, per frame, per stage
readdecode a video frame or read a dataset image
degradeapply the degradation
inferencethe ONNX Runtime session.run call alone
processingletterboxing, then decoding plus NMS
renderencode frames into the cache

Effective fps = 1000 / (read p50 + processing p50 + inference p50): the blue stages, the ones a deployed detector would run. The first 2 frames are warm-up and left out. A stage a run doesn't have shows as none, never 0 ms.

Swappable model runner

The detector sits behind a small runner interface. A deterministic stub runner stands in for YOLOX in the browser tests, so the UI is tested without model weights.

Typed API contract

The frontend's TypeScript types are generated from the backend's OpenAPI schema, and the check fails if they drift. The frontend runs no inference, matching or metrics; it draws from structured API data.

Runs from a fresh clone

The built frontend is committed and stamped with a digest of its sources; pytest fails if the bundle is stale. Reviewers need Python only: no Node.js, GPU or dataset for the demo.

Pinned and verified

Direct dependencies are pinned exactly, a constraints file freezes the full CPU install, and the model fetch script checks the weights' SHA-256.

Tested at three layers

700 pytest tests (19 of them need the real weights and run on request), Vitest unit tests for the frontend's pure logic, and 12 Playwright end-to-end specs with axe accessibility checks.

Local and private by design

The server binds to 127.0.0.1 only and never accepts a file path from the browser. No telemetry, cloud inference or third-party scripts. Dataset imagery is never redistributed.

Testing

  • Vitest
  • Playwright, axe-core

Limitations

  • Scope. Results hold for this SeeingThroughFog subset, YOLOX-Nano and this class mapping only.
  • Confounds. Weather co-occurs with lighting, road type and traffic, so a drop under "fog" mixes fog with everything else that differs.
  • Sim-to-real is distributional. Real-fog frames are different scenes from the clear frames, not paired frames.
  • Latency is this machine only, with the execution provider recorded. It is not a real-time claim.
  • Not for safety-critical use. It is an educational robustness evaluation, and it draws no automated conclusions.
